skill.name: youtube-thumbnail-design

content.value_statement: Small, cluttered thumbnails lose attention in crowded YouTube feeds. This skill provides practical design rules and image prompts for clear, mobile-ready concepts.
actual_capabilities: Defines recommended YouTube dimensions, aspect ratio, file size, and supported formats.
Applies safe zones for timestamps, chapter markers, progress bars, and device cropping.
Suggests high-contrast palettes, readable text limits, and focused thumbnail compositions.
Creates image-generation prompts for tutorials, comparisons, listicles, and face-focused designs.
Plans controlled A/B tests that change one visual variable per variant.
limitations: Image generation requires the external belt CLI, authentication, and network access.
The skill does not upload thumbnails or modify YouTube channel settings.
Generated images may require manual typography, branding, cropping, and file compression.
Design recommendations cannot guarantee higher click-through rates or viewer retention.

use_cases.title: Launch a New Video
use_cases.description: Create a clear thumbnail concept that matches the topic, title, and intended viewer emotion.

use_cases.title: Standardize Channel Visuals
use_cases.description: Define reusable contrast, text, face, and safe-zone rules across a publishing calendar.

use_cases.title: Test Competing Concepts
use_cases.description: Prepare controlled variants that isolate color, expression, text, background, or composition.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a YouTube thumbnail concept for [video topic]. Use one focal point, strong contrast, and no more than six text words.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting a thumbnail from a video topic

prompt_templates.title: Write an Image Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Write an image-generation prompt for [video topic] using [brand colors], a clear subject, dramatic lighting, and a mobile-readable composition.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Thumbnail
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this thumbnail description: [description]. Check safe zones, contrast, text length, focal point, mobile readability, and alignment with the video.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improving an existing concept before production

prompt_templates.title: Plan an A/B Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design two thumbnail variants for [video]. Keep all elements fixed except [test variable], and explain the hypothesis and evaluation criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Testing one visual variable with controlled variants

output_examples.input: Create a concept for a beginner coding tutorial.
output_examples.output: Use a bright laptop screen as the focal point, a curious face on the left, and the text START CODING in bold white.

output_examples.input: Plan an A/B test for a product comparison.
output: Variant A uses a warm yellow background.
Variant B uses a dark blue background.
Keep products, lighting, text, and composition identical.

output_examples.input: Review a thumbnail with eight words near the bottom-right corner.
output_examples.output: Reduce the text to six words or fewer and move it away from the duration overlay zone.

best_practices: Preview every concept at approximately 120 pixels wide before finalizing it.
Use one focal point, no more than three colors, and strong subject-background contrast.
Change only one variable between A/B test variants.
anti_patterns: Do not repeat the full video title as small thumbnail text.
Do not place faces, text, or essential details under interface overlays.
Do not use misleading imagery that conflicts with the video content.

faq.question: What dimensions should I use?
faq.answer: Use a 16:9 canvas at 1280 by 720 pixels minimum. A 1920 by 1080 canvas provides additional working detail.

faq.question: How much text should a thumbnail contain?
faq.answer: Use six words or fewer in a bold sans-serif style. Remove text when the image already communicates the idea.

faq.question: Does the skill generate finished thumbnails?
faq.answer: It can generate base images through belt. Final typography, branding, compression, and quality review may require a separate design tool.

faq.question: Why should I preview at 120 pixels?
faq.answer: Many viewers first see thumbnails at small mobile sizes. The preview reveals unreadable text, weak contrast, and unclear subjects.

faq.question: Can this guarantee a higher click-through rate?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on audience, topic, title, competition, and content quality. Use controlled tests to measure performance.

faq.question: Does the workflow send data to external services?
faq.answer: Yes. Belt commands authenticate with and send prompts to hosted image providers. Do not include confidential information in prompts.
